title: Cap. V Obj. 7 Sol: Gospel not inverted — Quisquis crediderit; elect get constant faith
pass_a_gloss: But let us come nearer to the reason proposed. We deny that from our position the Gospel is inverted, or that anything adverse to the Gospel is contained in it. The Gospel says, Whoever shall have believed will be saved: We say that God from special mercy inspires constant faith in certain ones whom he has decreed to lead through infallibly to life. The Gospel first commands faith, then under the condition of faith promises salvation: We teach that God first ordains some singular person to life, then truly pours faith into the heart of the same. I find here no fight or contradiction. The voice of the one evangelizing instructs individuals by what modes and means they may obtain eternal life: It therefore puts means first under a condition, to those who use which it promises the attainment. But the decree of God electing prefizes for certain persons both means and end, the end through means, and the means on account of the end; and therefore it is said to look to the end first and more principally, because on account of its infallible attainment such grace is conceived as prepared for such a person.
pass_b_english: Nearer then to their reason. We deny that our position inverts the Gospel or holds anything against it. The Gospel says Whoever believes will be saved; we say God from special mercy inspires constant faith in certain ones he has decreed to lead infallibly to life. The Gospel first commands faith, then under that condition promises salvation; we teach God first ordains a singular person to life, then pours faith into that heart. I find no fight or contradiction here. The evangelizing voice tells individuals by what means they may obtain eternal life — it puts means first under a condition and promises attainment to those who use them. But God's electing decree prefizes for certain persons both means and end — end through means, means for the end — and so is said to look to the end first and more principally, because for its infallible attainment such grace is conceived as prepared for that person.
source_text: Sed accedamus propius ad rationem propositam. Negamus ex sententia nostra Evangelium inverti, aut quicquam Evangelio adversum in ea contineri. Evangelium dicit, Quisquis crediderit, salvus erit: Nos dicimus, Deum ex speciali misericordia quibusdam, quos infallibiliter ad vitam perducere decrevit, fidem constantem inspirare. Evangelium prius mandat fidem, deinde sub conditione fidei salutem promittit: Nos docemus, Deum primo ordinare singularem aliquam personam ad vitam, deinde vero fidem cordi ejusdem infundere. Ego pugnam aut contradictionem hic nullam invenio. Vox Evangelizantis instituit singulos, quibus modis et mediis possint vitam aeternam consequi: Media igitur sub conditione praemittit, quibus reis consecutionem promittit. At decretum Dei eligentis praestituit certis personis et media et finem, finem per media, et media propter finem; atque idcirco dicitur finem prius et principalius respicere, quia propter infallibilem ejus adeptionem talem gratiam concipitur tali personae praeparare.
